definitions.explanation: A bullet or projectile fired from a gun. When read {弾|たま}, the character refers to ammunition; the same character is read {弾|だん} in compounds such as {弾丸|だんがん} (bullet).

examples.japanese: {弾|たま}を{込|こ}めて{構|かま}えた。
examples.english: I loaded a round and took aim.

examples.japanese: {撃|う}った{弾|たま}は{的|まと}を{外|はず}れ、{壁|かべ}に{当|あ}たった。
examples.english: The bullet I fired missed the target and hit the wall.

notes:
When read {弾|たま}, this character means a bullet or round of ammunition. The same sound is written {玉|たま} (ball, sphere) or {球|たま} (ball) for other senses — the {弾|たま} spelling specifically signals ammunition.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弾|たま}を{込|こ}める: to load a bullet
- {弾|たま}が{切|き}れる: to run out of ammunition
- {弾|たま}を{撃|う}つ: to fire a shot

RELATED WORDS:
- {弾丸|だんがん}: bullet — the standard compound noun ({音読|おんよ}み reading)
- {実弾|じつだん}: live ammunition
